newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strong growth seen for perishable goods cargo mark.
newsitem.headline: Strong growth seen for perishable goods cargo mark.

text.p: Perishable goods will become an increasingly important segment of the world air cargo market over the coming years, a senior freight forwarder forecast.
Gerald Kurz, newly-appointed perishable goods manager for Kuehne & Nagel International AG, said consumer demand in developed countries was driving intercontinental transport of fresh goods.
Perishable goods regularly transported by air included flowers, plants, fruit, vegetables, fresh meat and chocolate, he pointed out.

"Industrial nations have a rapidly-growing need for fresh produce. In particular, Western consumers expect a year-round supply with goods which are at best seasonally available in their home markets," Kurz said in a company statement.
"A fifth of the worldwide air cargo tonnage consists today of perishable goods, with a growing trend. Cooled sea, rail and truck transport comes on top of that," he added.
The major routes for such goods were Australia-Japan, South America to the U.S. and Europe, and southern and eastern Africa to Europe, Kurz said.
Perishables were a major export item for many countries with, for example, a high percentage of Columbian and Chilean exports comprising cut-flowers and fish for the U.S. market.
In 1996, Columbia exported some 150,000 tonnes of perishable goods while Chile with 70,000 tonnes, Kenya with 65,000 tonnes and South Africa with 55,000 tonnes were other major exporters.

Freight forwarders had the task of setting up complete "cool chains" from supplier to consignee and ensuring that such goods were transported correctly and rapidly, Kurz pointed out. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
